summary.headline: Patel Engineering FY26 revenue INR 5,103 crore (flat YoY); FY27 guided to grow 10% with order book at INR 15,119 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 5,102 crore versus INR 5,093 crore in FY25, with PAT up 21% to INR 294 crore. Q4 consolidated revenue was INR 1,421 crore with operating EBITDA of INR 215 crore (15.14% margin) and PAT of INR 71.5 crore versus INR 32.8 crore a year earlier. Gross debt fell to INR 1,187 crore from INR 1,645 crore after the rights issue, and debt-to-equity improved to 0.27 from 0.43. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of about 10%, with momentum expected to build from H2 FY27, and expects about INR 8,000 crore of new orders in FY27.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: 55% of FY26 revenue and 63% of order book at 31 Mar 2026; Subansiri Lower has four of eight units running (1,000 MW).

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: 23% of FY26 revenue and 16% of order book; Nira Deoghar canal won at INR 958 crore total (Patel share INR 192 crore).

segments.name: Tunnelling
segments.commentary: 17% of FY26 revenue and 5% of order book; CIDCO Treated Water Tunnel recorded 812 m in one month in January 2026 and about 6.2 km tunnelled in the quarter.

segments.name: Roads, urban infra and others
segments.commentary: 5% of FY26 revenue; urban infrastructure is 10% of order book and roads and others 6%. Kondhane Dam (CIDCO, about INR 1,300 crore) is the largest FY26 win.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 10%, with momentum expected to strengthen meaningfully from H2 FY27.
FY27 new order inflow expected at around INR 8,000 crore, supported by L1 position on INR 1,600 crore (Lower Arun, Nepal).
Subansiri Lower: all eight units expected to be operational in FY27.
Non-core asset monetisation target of INR 150-200 crore in FY27 (FY26 realised about INR 185 crore).
Interest cost expected to stay broadly flat in FY27 despite debt paydown, as new project advances of INR 700-800 crore come in.
Promoter pledge reduction target of around 15-20%, timing to be confirmed after lender discussions; OCD balance of INR 100-120 crore to be repaid over FY27-FY28.
capex_capacity: Subansiri Lower: four units (1,000 MW) operational after Unit-4 commissioning; civil work completed up to Unit 6; all eight units targeted in FY27.
Kiru and Kwar HEP in J&K are at full-scale concreting.
FY26 execution: over 13.5 lakh cubic metres of concreting and about 60,000 metric tonnes of reinforcement.
Current tender pipeline: about INR 6,000 crore submitted and under evaluation; INR 20,000 crore immediate pipeline; INR 40,000 crore to be bid over the next year.
demand_pricing: FY26 order inflow about INR 4,400 crore across hydropower, urban infrastructure, irrigation and other segments; order book INR 15,119 crore at 31 Mar 2026.

Major FY26 wins: Kondhane Dam about INR 1,300 crore (CIDCO), Renuka Ji Dam package about INR 900 crore (HPPCL), NEEPCO HEO 240 MW about INR 700 crore, Teesta-V about INR 240 crore (NHPC), Dorjilung Bhutan about INR 231 crore, and two coal mining packages totalling INR 798 crore (SECL, MDO model).
Management said it lost a large hydro project (Dibang, about INR 16,000-17,000 crore) to a new player that bid very low; hydro success ratio was 12-13% including it, 25-30% excluding it.
Pipeline cited: Sawalkote 1,856 MW, Kalai-II 1,200 MW, Kamala 1,720 MW, Upper Subansiri 1,600 MW, Etalin 3,000 MW; Kamala/Lower Subansiri bids expected in about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What hydro market share did the company achieve in FY26 wins, and why was the large Dibang-type project lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a success ratio of 12-13% including the large project (about INR 16,000-17,000 crore) and 25-30% excluding it; the loss was attributed to a new bidder pricing very low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and order outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue growth of about 10% and about INR 8,000 crore of new orders, based on the INR 1,600 crore L1 win and the INR 6,000 crore of tenders under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Why were exceptional items booked this quarter and is more pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is nothing further pending: a INR 56 crore impairment on hydro subsidiary investments and a INR 30 crore loss on the ACP Tollways stake (sale offer INR 55 crore, 32% stake) were booked; FY25 exceptional items related to the Vivad se Vishwas settlement of about INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost outlook and the blended rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost expected to stay broadly flat; blended average rate on debt and client advances 11-12%, with about INR 70 crore a year on non-fund-based limits.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-core monetisation and debt repayment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target INR 150-200 crore from land banks and arbitration awards; proceeds prioritised for term loan and OCD repayment, with OCD of INR 100-120 crore due over FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the promoter pledge reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm timeline; management plans to approach lenders after the March results and targets a reduction of around 15-20%, with an update expected next quarter.

risks_watch: Revenue growth has been flat (FY26 INR 5,102 crore vs FY25 INR 5,093 crore), and FY27 +10% depends on H2 execution ramp-up.
Competitive bidding with aggressive low bids from new entrants caused loss of large hydro projects.
Promoter pledge still elevated; promoter stake cited at 31.48% and promoter did not fully participate in the rights issue; timeline for pledge reduction not given.
Arbitration receivables of about INR 700 crore (over INR 400 crore in High Court) and balance about INR 2,300 crore; realisation timing of 5-7 years and only about INR 50 crore a year received.
Patel Smondo (Hyderabad) occupancy certificate pending and flat sales details not disclosed; service apartment operator not yet appointed.
Non-fund-based limits and client advances keep finance cost elevated (Q4 finance cost about INR 79 crore per investor question).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term pipeline and debt reduction, but evasive on timelines: promoter pledge reduction, land-bank sale timing and the Patel Smondo OC/flat-sale status were given without firm dates or numbers.
